title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Territorial Sea and the Contiguous Zone

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of exercising the sovereignty of the People's Republic of China over its territorial sea and the control over its contiguous zone, and safeguarding national security and maritime rights and interests.

Article 2 The territorial sea of the People's Republic of China is a belt of sea adjacent to the land territory and internal waters of the People's Republic of China.
The land territory of the People's Republic of China includes the mainland of the People's Republic of China and its coastal islands, Taiwan and its affiliated islands including the Diaoyu Islands, the Penghu Islands, the Dongsha Islands, the Xisha Islands, the Zhongsha Islands, the Nansha Islands, and all other islands belonging to the People's Republic of China.
The waters on the landward side of the baseline of the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China constitute the internal waters of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 The breadth of the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China is twelve nautical miles, measured from the baselines of the territorial sea.
The baselines of the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China are demarcated by the method of straight baselines, composed of straight lines connecting the adjacent base points.
The outer limit of the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China is the line every point of which is at a distance of twelve nautical miles from the nearest point of the baselines of the territorial sea.

Article 4 The contiguous zone of the People's Republic of China is a belt of sea adjacent to and beyond the territorial sea. The breadth of the contiguous zone is twelve nautical miles. The outer limit of the contiguous zone of the People's Republic of China is the line every point of which is at a distance of twenty-four nautical miles from the nearest point of the baselines of the territorial sea.
Article 5 The sovereignty of the People's Republic of China over its territorial sea extends to the air space over the territorial sea, as well as to the seabed and subsoil of the territorial sea.

Article 6 Foreign non-military ships enjoy the right of innocent passage through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China in accordance with law.
Foreign military ships entering the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China must be approved by the Government of the People's Republic of China.
Article 7 Foreign submarines and other underwater vehicles navigating through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China must navigate on the surface and display their flags.

Article 8 Foreign ships navigating through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China must comply with the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China and shall not impair the peace, security and good order of the People's Republic of China.
Foreign nuclear-powered ships and ships carrying nuclear substances, toxic substances or other dangerous substances navigating through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China must hold relevant certificates and take special precautionary measures.
The Government of the People's Republic of China has the right to take all necessary measures to prevent and stop non-innocent passage through the territorial sea.
Where foreign ships violate the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China, they shall be dealt with by the relevant organs of the People's Republic of China in accordance with law.

Article 9 For the maintenance of navigational safety and other special needs, the Government of the People's Republic of China may require foreign ships navigating through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China to use designated sea lanes or navigate in accordance with prescribed traffic separation schemes, and the specific measures shall be published by the Government of the People's Republic of China or the relevant competent authorities thereof.

Article 10 Where foreign military ships or foreign government ships operated for non-commercial purposes, when navigating through the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China, violate the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China, the relevant competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have the right to order them to leave the territorial sea immediately, and the flag State shall bear international responsibility for any loss or damage caused.

Article 11 Any international organization, foreign organization or individual conducting scientific research, marine operations or other activities in the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China must be approved by the Government of the People's Republic of China or the relevant competent authorities thereof, and shall comply with the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.
Where anyone, in violation of the preceding paragraph, illegally enters the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China for scientific research, marine operations or other activities, it shall be dealt with by the relevant organs of the People's Republic of China in accordance with law.

Article 12 Foreign aircraft may enter the air space over the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China only in accordance with the agreements or arrangements concluded between the government of that country and the Government of the People's Republic of China, or upon approval or acceptance by the Government of the People's Republic of China or an organ authorized thereby.

Article 13 The People's Republic of China has the right to exercise control in the contiguous zone to prevent and punish infringement of its laws and regulations concerning security, customs, finance, health or entry and exit administration within its land territory, internal waters or territorial sea.

Article 14 Where the relevant competent authorities of the People's Republic of China have good reason to believe that a foreign ship has violated the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China, they may exercise the right of hot pursuit against such foreign ship. Such pursuit must be commenced when the foreign ship or one of its small boats or other craft operating from the ship as a mother ship is within the internal waters, territorial sea or contiguous zone of the People's Republic of China. If the foreign ship is within the contiguous zone of the People's Republic of China, the pursuit may be undertaken only when the rights provided for in the relevant laws and regulations listed in Article 13 of this Law have been infringed. The pursuit may be continued outside the territorial sea or contiguous zone of the People's Republic of China so long as it is not interrupted. When the ship pursued enters its own territorial sea or the territorial sea of a third State, the pursuit terminates. The right of hot pursuit provided for in this Article shall be exercised by military ships, military aircraft or other ships and aircraft authorized by the Government of the People's Republic of China to perform government functions.
Article 15 The baselines of the territorial sea of the People's Republic of China shall be published by the Government of the People's Republic of China.
Article 16 The Government of the People's Republic of China shall formulate relevant provisions in accordance with this Law.
Article 17 This Law shall come into force on the date of its promulgation.
